model.name: Erlang-chain gametocyte maturation with n=5 sequestered immature compartments
model.equations: dI1/dt = alpha * A(t) - k * I1; dI2/dt = k * I1 - k * I2; dI3/dt = k * I2 - k * I3; dI4/dt = k * I3 - k * I4; dI5/dt = k * I4 - k * I5; dM/dt = k * I5 - gamma * M. A(t) = asexual parasites/mL linear interpolation; all states >= 0; units per mL.
model.driver_interpolation: Piecewise-linear interpolation of asexual density between supplied (time_days, asexual_parasites_per_ml) pairs, with constant extrapolation beyond [0, 26] days. Negative values clipped to zero.
model.solver: scipy.integrate.solve_ivp with method='LSODA' (automatic stiff/non-stiff switching), rtol=1e-8, atol=1e-10, max_step=0.1 day.
model.observation_model: Log-normal likelihood on log10(gametocytes/mL) with scale parameter sigma. Left-censored at 2 gametocytes/mL: contribution is log-CDF of the normal distribution.

diagnostics.alternative_model: n=1 exponential; NLL=2.39 (main NLL=6.05); predictions [t=10: 0.0; t=14: 0.2; t=21: 0.6; t=24: 0.7]
diagnostics.identifiability: With n=5 immature compartments, the production coefficient alpha and mean maturation time tau are partially confounded because both affect the amplitude of the mature-gametocyte peak. The number of compartments n cannot be uniquely identified from this profile; n=2-5 give similar NLL values. The single left-censored observation at day 5 provides limited information about the early rise. Mature clearance (gamma) and late-stage dynamics are better resolved from the post-peak decline (days 16-20), where asexual parasites are already cleared.
